1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value; and __maintaining the level of vacuum in the booster device at or above the predetermined value by modulating operation of the pump based on continuous monitoring of the vacuum level__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __and wherein the directional control valve is responsive to a vacuum sensor that detects when the level of vacuum reaches the predetermined value__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is actuated by a solenoid controlled by a vacuum sensing circuit__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __and wherein the solenoid is energized only when the vacuum level exceeds the predetermined value__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, __and wherein the directional control valve is controlled by a feedback control system that monitors vacuum pressure in real-time__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, __and periodically cleaning or replacing the filter based on a predetermined maintenance schedule__.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a vacuum sensor configured to continuously monitor the level of vacuum in the booster device__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __wherein the directional control valve is controlled by a control circuit responsive to signals from the vacuum sensor__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __and wherein the directional control valve includes a solenoid actuator controlled by the control circuit__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __and wherein the solenoid actuator is energized only when the vacuum sensor detects that the vacuum level has reached the predetermined value__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __and wherein the control circuit includes logic to prevent pump operation when the vacuum level is at or above the predetermined value__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __and a filter maintenance indicator that signals when the filter requires cleaning or replacement__.

13. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; __a vacuum sensor configured to continuously monitor the level of vacuum in the booster device__; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a control circuit responsive to the vacuum sensor__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced, __wherein the directional control valve is controlled by the control circuit to modulate pump operation based on real-time vacuum monitoring__.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __and wherein the directional control valve includes a solenoid actuator controlled by the control circuit__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __and wherein the solenoid actuator is energized only when the vacuum sensor detects that the vacuum level has reached the predetermined value__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __and wherein the control circuit includes logic to prevent pump operation when the vacuum level is at or above the predetermined value__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __and a filter maintenance indicator that signals when the filter requires cleaning or replacement__.

19. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type, __and wherein the control circuit is configured to optimize pump operation based on engine load and vacuum demand__.
